visual_action: Former President Jimmy Carter is interviewed by talk show host Stephen Colbert on the set of a late-night show. The clip consists of them talking while seated across from each other at a desk. The camera cuts between a two-shot and close-ups of each man speaking.

cast.name: Jimmy Carter
cast.evidence: He is the main subject of the interview clip, and the on-screen text wishes him a 'Happy 100th birthday'.

cast.name: Stephen Colbert
cast.evidence: He is shown interviewing Jimmy Carter. The source of the clip is identified as 'The Late Show'.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: Colbert asks Carter, 'Do you pray for Donald Trump?' Carter's witty response about praying for him is the focus of the clip.

on_screen_text.text: Happy 100th birthday to President Jimmy Carter 💙
Do you pray for Donald Trump?
I pray that he'll be a good president
and that he'll keep our country at peace,
and that he'll refrain from using nuclear weapons,
and that he will promote human rights.
thank you for your prayers, first of all.
Do you think your prayers are being answered so far?
Well, I used to have a pastor who would say,
"When you pray, God has three answers.
and the third one is, 'You gotta be kidding.'"
So I'm not sure which one it is yet.

spoken_summary: Stephen Colbert asks former President Jimmy Carter if he prays for then-President Donald Trump. Carter outlines his prayers for Trump to be a good president, keep peace, and promote human rights. When Colbert asks if his prayers are being answered, Carter tells an anecdote about a pastor who said God has three answers to prayers: 'Yes,' 'No,' and 'You gotta be kidding.' Carter humorously concludes, 'I'm not sure which one it is yet,' implying God's answer to his prayers for Trump is 'You gotta be kidding.'
audio_music: The audio consists solely of the dialogue between the speakers and the sounds of a live studio audience laughing and applauding at Carter's joke.
editing_pacing: The video is a single, unedited clip from a television interview, primarily featuring talking heads. It cuts between a wide shot of both speakers and medium close-ups of each person as they talk.
emotions_signaled: Admiration (for Jimmy Carter's wit and grace)
Mockery (directed at Donald Trump through Carter's anecdote)
cultural_references: The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
central_claim: Jimmy Carter uses a witty religious anecdote to subtly criticize Donald Trump, suggesting that his prayers for Trump's success as a president are so unlikely to be answered that the response from God would be 'You gotta be kidding.'
intended_effect: To celebrate Jimmy Carter's wisdom and humor while encouraging the viewer to laugh at the implied criticism of Donald Trump.
